yaml.author: Anh Lam

markdown.markdown:
```{r} #| include: false library(tidyverse) library(haven) library(knitr) demo_raw <- read_xpt("data/P_DEMO.xpt") deq_raw <- read_xpt("data/P_DEQ.xpt") dashboard_data <- demo_raw %>% select(SEQN, RIDSTATR, RIDAGEYR, RIAGENDR, RIDRETH3, DMDEDUC2) %>% left_join( deq_raw %>% select(SEQN, DED120, DED125, DEQ034D), by = "SEQN" ) %>% filter( RIDSTATR == 2, RIDAGEYR >= 20, RIDAGEYR <= 59 ) %>% mutate( DED120 = replace(DED120, DED120 %in% c(3333, 7777, 9999), NA), DMDEDUC2 = replace(DMDEDUC2, DMDEDUC2 %in% c(7, 9), NA), DEQ034D = replace(DEQ034D, DEQ034D %in% c(7, 9), NA), outdoor_workday = DED120, gender = factor( RIAGENDR, levels = c(1,2), labels = c("Male", "Female") ), education = case_when( DMDEDUC2 %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Less than high school", DMDEDUC2 == 3 ~ "High school or GED", DMDEDUC2 == 4 ~ "Some college or AA", DMDEDUC2 == 5 ~ "College graduate or above", TRUE ~ NA_character_ ), education = factor( education, levels = c( "Less than high school", "High school or GED", "Some college or AA", "College graduate or above" ) ), regular_sunscreen = case_when( DEQ034D %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Regular", DEQ034D %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Not Regular", TRUE ~ NA_character_ ) ) %>% filter( !is.na(outdoor_workday), !is.na(education) ) regular_pct <- dashboard_data %>% filter(!is.na(regular_sunscreen)) %>% summarize( pct = mean(regular_sunscreen == "Regular") * 100 ) %>% pull(pct) ``` ## Row

This dashboard explores outdoor time and sun protection behaviors among adults ages 20–59 using NHANES data.

## Row {height="20%"} ### Participants ```{r} #| content: valuebox list( title = "Participants", value = "4,867", subtitle = "Adults ages 20–59", icon = "people" ) ``` ### Median Outdoor Time ```{r} #| content: valuebox list( title = "Median Outdoor Time", value = "60 min", subtitle = "On a work or school day", icon = "clock" ) ``` ### Regular Sunscreen Use ```{r} #| content: valuebox list( title = "Regular Sunscreen Users", value = paste0(round(regular_pct, 1), "%"), subtitle = "Use sunscreen always or most of the time", icon = "sun" ) ``` ## Row {height="55%"} ### Outdoor Time by Education ```{r} #| echo: false #| fig-height: 3.5 #| fig-width: 8 ggplot( dashboard_data, aes(x = education, y = outdoor_workday) ) + geom_boxplot() + coord_flip() + labs( title = "Outdoor Time by Education Level", x = NULL, y = "Outdoor time (minutes)" ) + theme_minimal() + theme( plot.title = element_text(size = 13), axis.text = element_text(size = 9), axis.title = element_text(size = 10) ) ``` # Sunscreen Use ## Row {heigh="60%"} ### Regular Sunscreen Use by Gender ```{r} #| echo: false #| fig-height: 3.5 #| fig-width: 5.5 sunscreen_gender <- dashboard_data %>% filter( !is.na(gender), !is.na(regular_sunscreen) ) %>% count(gender, regular_sunscreen) %>% group_by(gender) %>% mutate(percent = n / sum(n) * 100) %>% ungroup() ggplot( sunscreen_gender, aes( x = gender, y = percent, fill = regular_sunscreen ) ) + geom_col(position = "dodge") + labs( title = "Regular Sunscreen Use by Gender", x = NULL, y = "Percent", fill = "Sunscreen Use" ) + theme_minimal() + theme( plot.title = element_text(size = 13), axis.text = element_text(size = 9), axis.title = element_text(size = 10), legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.text = element_text(size = 9) ) ``` ### Sunscreen Use Summary ```{r} #| echo: false sunscreen_gender %>% filter(regular_sunscreen == "Regular") %>% select(gender, percent) %>% mutate( percent = paste0(round(percent, 1), "%") ) %>% rename( Gender = gender, `Regular Sunscreen Use` = percent ) %>% kable() ``` # Predicting ## Row {height="45%"} ### Model Performance ```{r} #| echo: false model_performance <- tibble( Model = c("Big Model", "Small Model"), RMSPE = c(157.152, 165.532), MAE = c(100.461, 104.731), `Validated R²` = c(0.138, 0.046) ) model_performance %>% knitr::kable( digits = 2, caption = "Test Data Performance" ) ``` ### Key Finding The Big Model had lower prediction error and a higher $R^2$ than the Smaller Model. However, both models had significant prediction errors, which suggests that education and the demographic and sunscreen variables explain only a limited amount of variation in outdoor time. # About the Data ## Row {height="50%"} ### Data This dashboard uses data from the **NHANES 2017–March 2020 Pre-Pandemic cycle**. The analysis focuses on adults ages 20–59 who completed the examination. The dashboard examines outdoor time on work or school days, education level, gender, and regular sunscreen use. ### Variables **Outdoor Time:** Minutes spent outdoors on a typical work or school day. **Education:** Less than high school, High school/GED, Some college/AA, or College graduate or above. **Gender:** Male or Female. **Regular Sunscreen Use:** Participants who reported using sunscreen always or most of the time were classified as regular sunscreen users. ```{=html} ```
